passage: At the crowded bus stop, honking drowned half of what the man said. "I'm a friend of your uncle," he shouted, smiling. "He sent me to take you home." Uma looked at him. Her mother's brother, Chinmay Mama, had told her that anyone he sent would know the family word. "Which uncle? What's his name?" she asked. "The tall one... you know." "And the family word?" His smile stiffened. Uma took a step back, then another. "No thank you," she said, and moved toward the ticket counter, where a clerk watched the queue. The man turned away into the noise. Uma told the clerk everything. The clerk phoned Chinmay Mama and stayed with her until he came.

qa.q: What two things did Uma ask the man for?
qa.a: She asked his friend's name and the family word.

qa.q: What was Uma feeling when the man could not give the family word?
qa.a: Uneasy and suspicious, since the story did not fit, so she stepped back and left.

qa.q: What else could Uma do if the man kept following her, and why?
qa.a: She could speak loudly and go closer to the clerk and the queue, because many people nearby make it easier to get help.

qa.q: How might the clerk see Uma's report?
qa.a: The clerk takes it seriously and sees a sensible child, so the clerk phones Chinmay Mama and stays with her.

grounding: A girl notices that a stranger claiming to know her uncle cannot give his name or the family word, and stays away.

passage: At the gate of her Kolkata school, a man came up to Yamini. "I'm a friend of your uncle's. He asked me to pick you up." Yamini's mother had told her that only Chaitanya Mama or her parents would ever collect her. "What's my uncle's name?" she asked. The man laughed. "Your uncle, you know. Come on." "What's our family word?" He shrugged. Yamini noticed his story didn't fit. A real friend would know Mama's name. She stepped back through the gate and went to the school office. "A man says my uncle sent him, but he doesn't know my uncle's name." The clerk kept her in the office and called her mother, who came herself and reported it to the principal that day.

qa.q: Who had Yamini's mother said would collect her?
qa.a: Only Chaitanya Mama or her parents.

qa.q: What made Yamini feel suspicious about the man?
qa.a: She felt uneasy because his story didn't fit: he didn't know her uncle's name or the family word.

qa.q: What else could Yamini do if no office was open?
qa.a: She could stay with a teacher or the guard inside the gate and ask them to call her parents.

qa.q: How does the news look to Yamini's mother?
qa.a: Her mother takes it seriously, comes herself and reports it the same day, and is probably proud and shaken.

grounding: It shows a girl noticing a stranger claiming to be her uncle's friend does not know his name or the code word, and staying away.

passage:
"Jahnavi! Come, your uncle sent me."
"Which uncle?"
"Your uncle. Come, the car's here."
"What's his name?"
"Beta, don't waste time."
"Then what's our word? My uncle always tells people the word."
"Word? What word?"
Jahnavi stepped back behind the school gate.
"Saurabh sir!"
Her teacher came out of the staffroom. "What's wrong?"
"That man says my uncle sent him. He doesn't know my uncle's name. Or the word."
The man was already walking away. Saurabh sir kept Jahnavi beside him, called her parents, and told the principal, who called the police that afternoon.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi say her uncle always tells people?
How did Jahnavi feel when the man couldn't answer?
qa.a: She felt suspicious and alarmed, enough to step back behind the gate and call her teacher.

qa.q: Which step protected Jahnavi most, and what else should she remember?
qa.a: She tested the story and went to a teacher; she could also remember to never go toward a car, even to see who is inside.

qa.q: How does the incident look to Saurabh sir?
qa.a: Saurabh sir sees a child at risk and acts quickly, keeping her close, calling her parents and telling the principal.

grounding: It shows a girl noticing a stranger's story does not fit because he knows neither her uncle's name nor the family's code word, and staying away.
